newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Debt vols in neutral as US payrolls loom.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Debt vols in neutral as US payrolls loom.

text.p: Options trade on LIFFE was subdued on Thursday and implied volatility firm after the fireworks of recent days and ahead of U.S. October jobs data, traders said.

"People are wating to see what is going to happen tomorrow," said Steven West, options trader at GNI in London. "Having been caught on the hop in sterling yesterday, people are saying "who knows where the non-farm payrolls are going to be?'."
"Volatility is staying firm," he said. "Locals this morning attempted to push it down so they could buy it back up again but they didn't get very far."
Locals work their own books as opposed to banks and institutions which trade for clients.

Traders said volatility was around Wednesday's closing levels. LIFFE data show December 99.50 Bund calls at 4.75 percent and December 110-00 gilt calls at 7.51 percent. March 93.75 short sterling calls ended Wednesday at 11.42 pct.
December Bunds were quoted at 99.66 at 1147 GMT, up 18 basis points from Wednesday, gilts were up 6/32 at 109-23 and March short sterling was at 93.53, down 0.03.

Bond options markets were caught off guard on Wednesday when Britain rasied base rates by a 1/4 point to 6.0 percent. It has been a fullsome week for the market, with hefty U.S. indicators such as the employment cost index and third quarter GDP giving Treasuries a reason to rally.
October non-farm payrolls are due on Friday.
"In the Bund it's very, very quiet," Tom Chlada, senior trader at Nationsbank Europe in London.

"Yesterday, the order of the day was a very bullish tone. Some of the large houses were buying the par (100.00 strike) calls in good quantities and also buying the par calls and selling the 99.00 puts," he said, adding trade in these combinations amounted to around 6,500 lots.
When the U.S. market pulled back late Wednseday on strong new home sales, trade tapered down and has remained quiet since, he said.

"The Bund has been in such a tight range between 99.05 and 99.94 for a month or so that it's looking for a reason to break out," Chlada said. "The T-bond rallied but the Bunds did not take it to the next level and everyone's looking for that."
